analysis:
This PR is documentation-only: docs/reference/configuration.md and docs/threat-model.yaml. No executable source changed, and the add-on hold code (Addon/, LifecycleMailbox.swift) was not supplied.

configuration.md: the DARKBLOOM_ADDON_SOCKET row now says every build reads the variable, although it is described as tests-only. The settle-bound constant is renamed to addonHoldSettleTimeoutDefault, and a load that outlives it is waited for rather than abandoned. The shown excerpt (lines 672-752) covers the prefix-cache section and is unrelated to the add-on change.

threat-model.yaml: TB-012 adds the operator lifecycle mailbox, accept-time peer verification before slot allocation, request limits (10 s and 8 KiB per request line, 300 s idle), the socket-override behavior and the mailbox's 60-second validity. It also adds the model-load fence and several limitations: no bound on a held machine lock, a fail-open hold record, a connection flood delaying the add-on, and self-reported busy fields. The T-059 mitigation text is extended. New T-060 (DoS from starving the add-on socket or stalling control-file reads, affecting A-018) is rated low, with mitigations implemented and the flood residual marked accepted.

The PR openly records the weaknesses it describes (fail-open hold record, same-UID boundary, unbounded lock-held hold, DARKBLOOM_ADDON_SOCKET honored in all builds). I found no invalidated threat assumption, no weakened documented control, and no inconsistency with the supplied canonical TB-002/TB-003 text. The patch excerpt for the YAML is truncated, but the base and patch units cover the changed hunks.

Open question for later review: the claims in the YAML, including accept-time verification, O_NONBLOCK/O_NOFOLLOW opens, the model-load fence and the mailbox's process-identity binding, are unverified against code. Reviewers of the corresponding source PR should check them. Also check that an unforced release is refused while the machine lock is held, and that DARKBLOOM_ADDON_SOCKET, honored in every build, cannot be abused by a same-UID environment to redirect the hold record or lock.
